title: Sell Mineral Rights in Star City, WV

metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Star City, WV
metaDescription: Star City, Monongalia County mineral owners: Morgantown-adjacent development, severed residential-lot minerals, and courthouse title checks.
heroLead: Star City sits just outside Morgantown in Monongalia County, where residential and commercial growth has built up over mineral estates severed well before the current development existed.
intro: As part of the greater Morgantown area, Star City has seen substantial residential and commercial buildout over the past several decades, while the mineral acreage underneath much of that development continues to be tracked separately through the Monongalia County Courthouse's older deed records.

sections.heading: Development built over severed minerals
paragraphs: Owning property in Star City doesn't necessarily mean owning what's beneath it — many mineral estates here were severed from the surface generations before the current buildings existed, leaving the mineral owner and the surface owner as entirely separate parties tracked under different chains of title.

sections.heading: Proximity to early Marcellus leasing
paragraphs: Star City's location close to Morgantown put it within reach of the county's early Marcellus leasing activity, which means some tracts here carry lease history going back over a decade, potentially with more favorable or less favorable terms than more recent leasing rounds depending on when the original agreement was signed.

sections.heading: What an early Marcellus lease's primary term means today
paragraphs: Star City-area leases signed during the county's early leasing wave typically included a primary term of several years, after which the lease needed to be held by production or it would expire. More than a decade later, confirming whether your lease is still validly held by production — rather than technically expired but never formally released — is worth checking.
This status affects both what you're owed going forward and what a buyer would pay for the interest today.

faqs.question: Do I own minerals under my Star City property?
faqs.answer: Not automatically — check your deed for a mineral reservation, or have a courthouse records search confirm whether the minerals were severed by a previous owner.

faqs.question: How old is a typical Star City-area lease?
faqs.answer: Some trace back to the county's early Marcellus leasing wave, potentially over a decade old, which is worth checking against current terms.

faqs.question: Can I find out if my family holds a severed interest near Star City?
faqs.answer: Yes, a Monongalia County Courthouse records search under your family name will confirm whether such an interest exists.

faqs.question: How do I know if my early Star City-area lease is still validly held by production?
faqs.answer: Check the well's current production status against your lease's held-by-production language, or request a courthouse and operator records check.

faqs.question: Is Star City close enough to Morgantown to share in its Marcellus leasing history?
faqs.answer: Yes, given the proximity, Star City-area tracts were often included in the same early leasing waves that touched Morgantown and the surrounding county.
